source: language_cases_lore.txt and language_cases_session.txt in this folder: invented text for DMbot's tests, written for #4229 (the session reader of languages; Supervisor's ruling A). Every name and line is made up; the four player characters are the sample's, by name only, so sample_run can say who plays each.

how_to_read.languages: a character's languages heard in the session (#4229): {character, language, line, note, doc}; scored as found, missed, and extra (a language row the key does not list). A language a character with no sheet is heard using waits as a question for the DM (#4229 1c) until accepted, so score after the run's accept step.
how_to_read.must_not_languages: lines that must give no language to anyone: a language named but not spoken (runes), one a character can't speak, a question, and a line with no language. One kept is counted as extra by the check.
how_to_read.line: the line of the session file that holds it; blank lines count

languages.note: heard used: 'Okthandom answers her in Dwarvish'
heard used: the DM says she answers in Dwarvish
heard used: 'mutters a curse in Halfling'
misheard: speech to text wrote 'Elfish'; the language is Elvish

must_not_languages.note: named but not spoken: runes on a door are Elvish; nobody speaks it here
can't speak: Cerric doesn't speak Giant
a question: nobody is said to speak Orc
